name: Utensil Recognition
description: Dataset for recognizing utensils from images. Given a photo and a prompt, the model must output the correct utensil category. It evaluates multi-class object recognition on everyday kitchen tools.
card_text: The Utensil Recognition dataset contains 190 image–text samples. Each sample pairs a photograph of a single utensil or kitchen tool with a fixed instruction, 'recognize the utensil in the image'. The expected output is a single uppercase category label such as KITCHEN_KNIFE or POTATO_PEELER. Images are everyday object photos, typically showing one dominant utensil. The task is closed-set multi-class classification: models read the image and the instruction, then predict the utensil class. No bounding boxes, segmentation masks, multiple-choice options, or free-form explanations are provided. The dataset assumes each image contains one recognizable utensil and that the category vocabulary is fixed. It targets basic visual object recognition in a kitchen-tool domain.

image.semantics: Photograph of a single utensil or kitchen tool, such as a knife or peeler. It is the visual input that the model must recognize.

question.semantics: Fixed textual instruction asking the model to recognize the utensil shown in the image. It specifies the task and directs attention to the image.

answer.semantics: Target utensil category label in uppercase snake_case, e.g., KITCHEN_KNIFE or POTATO_PEELER. It is the correct class for the pictured object.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample contains an image reference (input.image_file), a fixed textual instruction (input.prompt), and a single utensil category label (output.prediction). The image provides the visual object to recognize; the prompt asks the model to identify that utensil; the answer is the correct utensil class name. No bounding boxes, masks, options, or dialogs are present.
